sentences.show: Britain's greatest admiral won its greatest sea battle, and came home in a barrel of brandy.
The Battle of Trafalgar was fought on this day in 1805.
Horatio Nelson had 27 ships. France and Spain had 33.
Instead of lining up, he drove straight into their line, in two columns.
First, a signal: "England confides that every man will do his duty."
His signal officer suggested "expects". It was in the code book. "Confides" would have to be spelt out.
In the fighting, a French musket ball struck Nelson in the shoulder, and lodged near his spine.
18 enemy ships were captured or destroyed. Britain lost none.
Below deck, Nelson murmured: "Thank God I have done my duty."
He died three hours after he was hit.
For the voyage home, his body was kept in a cask of brandy, for a hero's funeral in London.
Also on this day: Florence Nightingale set off for the Crimean War, and New York's Guggenheim Museum opened.
